subject: general
question: In February 2021, which of the following was amended, enabling the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to also look after the development of Ropeways and Alternate Mobility Solutions?

options.text: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1951
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1981
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1971

solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In February 2021, the **Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961** was amended to include the development and regulation of Ropeways and Alternate Mobility Solutions under the ambit of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH).
 
• Prior to the amendment, the development of ropeways was under the Ministry of Railways.
 
• With the change, MoRTH became responsible for the development, construction, and maintenance of ropeways as a mode of transportation, enhancing connectivity in hilly and remote areas.
 
• This amendment aimed to facilitate faster implementation of ropeway projects and streamline decision-making processes.
 
• Ropeways are considered an eco-friendly and sustainable mode of transport, especially in difficult terrains, and play a crucial role in boosting tourism and local economies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961:**

 
 
• These rules were formulated under Article 77(3) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They allocate various subjects and responsibilities to different Ministries and Departments of the Government of India.
 
• The objective is to ensure a structured and efficient governance system.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH):**
 
 
• MoRTH is responsible for the development of road infrastructure and transport systems in India.
 
• It oversees policies related to highways, road safety, and motor vehicles.
 
• With the amendment, MoRTH's scope was expanded to include ropeways and alternate mobility solutions.
 
 
 
• **Ropeways:**
 
 
• Ropeways are aerial transportation systems that use cables for movement, mainly used in hilly terrains and tourist destinations.
 
• They are cost-effective, environment-friendly, and provide a safer alternative to traditional roads in challenging terrains.
 
• India has several operational ropeways, such as those in Auli, Gulmarg, and Darjeeling.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Mobility Solutions:**
 
 
• These refer to innovative and sustainable modes of transportation, including ropeways, cable cars, and other low-emission systems.
 
• They aim to reduce traffic congestion, support eco-friendly travel, and improve connectivity in remote areas.
 
• Alternate mobility solutions are gaining traction globally as a means to tackle urban mobility challenges.
